terminal_record.title: Rosen Contacted Manhattan Prosecutors After Manafort’s Lawyer Raised Rikers Concerns
terminal_record.description_short: Jeffrey Rosen sought Manhattan prosecutors’ views after Manafort’s lawyer asked that he remain in federal custody over Rikers concerns.
terminal_record.description_medium: NBC News reported that Paul Manafort’s lawyer asked federal officials to keep him in federal custody because of health and safety concerns about Rikers Island. Deputy Attorney General Jeffrey Rosen sent Manhattan prosecutors the lawyer’s letter and asked for their views. Their office said it made no housing recommendation; Manafort stayed in federal custody in Manhattan.
terminal_record.description_long: In June 2019, as Manhattan prosecutors prepared a state case against Paul Manafort, his lawyer asked the Bureau of Prisons to keep him in federal custody, citing health and personal-safety concerns about Rikers Island. NBC News obtained a letter Deputy Attorney General Jeffrey Rosen sent to Manhattan prosecutors with the defense letter attached; Rosen asked whether the office had a response. District Attorney Cyrus Vance replied that his office had made no recommendation about where Manafort should be housed and took no position among Rikers, another city facility, or the Metropolitan Correctional Center. Federal officials ultimately kept Manafort in federal custody at the Manhattan facility while making him available to state prosecutors. The reporting supports DOJ involvement after a defense request, followed by consultation with prosecutors and a stated health-and-safety rationale. It does not establish that DOJ independently ordered Manafort kept out of Rikers, that prosecutors opposed the arrangement, or that President Trump directed the decision. The prior title’s claim of a Trump DOJ order therefore overstates the documented sequence.
terminal_record.date_precision: day; federal officials informed Manhattan prosecutors on Monday, June 17, 2019, as reported by NBC News on June 18.

terminal_record.description_short: The frozen entry alleges a February 2025 threat against Mark Milley and James Mattis; the supplied material does not verify it.
terminal_record.description_medium: The frozen entry alleges that Trump threatened court-martials of retired generals Mark Milley and James Mattis in February 2025. The supplied packet has no contemporaneous statement, directive or case record supporting the allegation. Its Reuters link concerns a separate January 28 action involving Milley and does not corroborate a February threat. The exact wording, date, legal analysis, reaction and any proceedings remain unresolved.
terminal_record.description_long:
An earlier Trump Files entry alleges that in February 2025 Donald Trump threatened to seek court-martials for retired generals Mark Milley and James Mattis after they criticized him. The supplied synopsis also says that legal experts viewed the retired officers as protected from court-martial for post-retirement speech, and that the reported threats drew condemnation and could chill future dissent. Those claims are carried forward from the supplied entry; this packet includes no contemporaneous threat, exact quotation, identified legal expert or source for the described public reaction. The record therefore does not establish that a threat was made or that either officer faced proceedings.

The only linked report identified in the supplied review is a January 28, 2025 Reuters item about Pentagon actions involving Milley’s security clearance, security detail and a review of his retired rank. The review identifies that as a separate event, not corroboration of the alleged February threat or a claim about Mattis. The Reuters page returned HTTP 401 in the prior review, so its contents are not independently assessed here. The exact date, wording, legal basis, response and outcome of the alleged threat remain unknown. This internal draft records the allegation and its evidence gap; it is not publication eligible.
